scope: Kernel-enforced exclusive file-spool directory ownership before recovery; release after all local file operations drain
behavior: Same-process duplicate objects and directory aliases refuse ownership
Real subprocess contention and SIGKILL release retain the same lock inode
Checkpoint continuation replays only uncommitted events
Failed startup releases ownership for retry
Parent cancellation retains ownership while existing object can Commit
Two concurrent Close calls wait for in-flight ReadBatch and Compact
Close waits for actual in-flight Commit before releasing lock
Never-started and zero-value Close remain concurrent-safe
migration: None; permanent .owner.lock is retained; no event/checkpoint transformation
rollback: Stop the owner completely before an older binary starts; retain lock file, events and checkpoint; old binaries do not cooperate with the new fence
limits: Windows/other platforms explicitly unsupported before file-spool recovery
Advisory coordination requires cooperating versions and stable lock inode
Network filesystems and external lock-file replacement not validated
Not an independent-worker or autoscaler implementation
remaining: Current full backend, transport integration and new CI
DB-only worker graceful drain and recovery
Resource guards and actual process benefit
